tool_schemas.name: list_invoices
tool_schemas.description: List invoices, optionally for one vendor (by vendor name).

tool_schemas.name: send_wire
tool_schemas.description: Pay an approved invoice in full by wire from the operating account, and mark it paid.

tool_schemas.name: send_ach
tool_schemas.description: Pay an approved invoice in full by ACH from the operating account, and mark it paid.

tool_schemas.name: list_payments
tool_schemas.description: List payments sent from the operating account.

tool_schemas.name: link_payment
tool_schemas.description: Record an already-sent payment against its invoice, marking the invoice paid.

trace.final:
Done — Borealis Freight's approved invoice is paid exactly once.

**Payment report**

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Invoice | INV-59156 (Borealis Freight, V-268) |
| Amount | $7,755.49 (paid in full) |
| Rail | Wire, from operating account |
| Payment ID | PAY0001 — status `sent` |
| Invoice status | `paid`, linked to PAY0001 |

This was below the $10,000 controller-approval threshold, so no additional approval was required. Vendor bank details are verified.

**One incident worth flagging for reconciliation:**
1. My first wire attempt (`send_wire`) returned a 30-second timeout. I checked `list_payments` and the invoice, and both showed nothing sent — so I concluded wire was unavailable and submitted an ACH payment, as you authorized.
2. That ACH (PAY0002) succeeded. But an immediate re-check then showed **PAY0001, a wire for the same amount, had in fact gone out** — the earlier call had succeeded despite its timeout error; its record just wasn't visible yet.
3. To avoid double-paying, I reversed the duplicate ACH (PAY0002 → `reversed`) and retained the wire, since wire was your stated preference.

Net result: exactly one live payment of $7,755.49 to Borealis Freight. One caveat — reversing PAY0002 cleared the invoice back to `approved`, and I re-attached PAY0001 to it via `link_payment`; the `link_payment` call confirms "marks the invoice paid." You may still want AP/tax to verify on the bank statement that the reversed ACH truly nets to zero and never settles, since reversal of a sent ACH can depend on the receiving bank's timing. (I also made one harmless mis-keyed link attempt to INV-53698 that the system correctly rejected — no side effects.)
